Random swaps of the history features while training

Source: R/imputeLongitudinal.R
history_dropout_inputs.Rd

With history = TRUE, a subject never measured for a biomarker has history features (count 0, a stand-in level) that the network almost never sees while training, since every training row with that biomarker observed comes from a subject who was measured. Faced with them at imputation it extrapolated: in simulations it took the stand-in for the subject's own level, imputed with too little spread, and biased the fitted coefficients (the event-time coefficient by about 40%). Training therefore swaps, at random, a row's history features for one biomarker with their "unseen" version (see history_features()), keeping the row's own values as targets, so the network learns to impute that biomarker from the covariates and the other biomarkers alone. Each biomarker's rate is the share of rows from subjects never measured for it, at least 10%, and 0 (no swaps, as before) when every subject has some value of it.

Usage

history_dropout_inputs(X_cov, X_unseen, columns, rate)

Arguments

X_cov

Network inputs (standardized), a torch tensor.

X_unseen

The same inputs with every biomarker's history replaced by its "unseen" version, standardized identically.

columns

List with, per biomarker, the columns of its history features in X_cov.

rate

Per-biomarker swap probability.

Value

A function of a row index tensor (or NULL for every row) returning the inputs with fresh random swaps, or NULL when every rate is 0.
